newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's Jyske Bank H1 profits soar.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's Jyske Bank H1 profits soar.

text.p: Jyske Bank, Denmark's fourth-biggest bank, on Wednesday reported first half pre-tax earnings up 27 percent over the same period last year and well in excess of analysts' expectations.

Announcing a first-half ordinary pre-tax result of 505 million crowns ($88.4 million) , compared to 397 million during the first six months of 1995, Jyske Bank said interest margins fell, but lending and borrowing increased, leaving net interest receipts largely unaltered.
In a statement accompanying its interim result, Jyske Bank described its first-half 1996 performance as "satisfactory".
It reiterated earlier estimates for the full year, adding that earnings from lending would go on rising in the second half of 1996 but less so than in the year's first six months.

"The group budget for 1996 is expected to be fulfilled with core activity earnings in the 950 million-1.050 billion crown range, loss and bad debt provisions between 300-350 million crowns and pre-tax, securities, forex and extraordinary items profit at the upper end of the 600-750 million crown range," Jyske said.
The result was better than average analyst expectations of a 420 million crown ordinary pre-tax interim profit.
In 1995 Jyske Bank posted whole year net profits of 725 million crowns compared to 1994's 90 million crowns.
Jyske Bank was the last of Denmark's four big banks to announce its first-half 1996 results. All of the banks generally reported solid advances on the same 1995 period.
